title: Single life
hook: a single person has a full place in the sangat
tomorrow: Bebe twisted her ankle in the garden. who takes care of her now?

segments.voice: Yesterday, every kind of family, all in one row at langar, because all are children of the One. Every family. Now, one person on her own.

At Jasleen's wedding, Bhua Kiran, Simran's dad's sister, got asked the same question by aunty after aunty: so, when is your turn? She laughed every time, passed the sweets, and danced at the bhangra. Simran watched her face, and didn't laugh. Now Bhua Kiran is the one asking at the dinner table, half joking: where exactly do I fit? And Simran is stuck on something odd she noticed at the wedding. The Lavan, the four wedding hymns, are by Guru Ram Das. So why does the Guru write as the bride? And why do the Gurus keep calling themselves the soul-bride, all through the Guru Granth Sahib?
screen: `AUNTY AFTER AUNTY: WHEN IS YOUR TURN?` → `WHERE DOES BHUA KIRAN FIT?` → `WHY DOES THE GURU WRITE AS A BRIDE?`

segments.voice: Here's the answer, and it's the part to tell a friend. In Gurbani, the bride isn't a woman on her wedding day. The bride is the soul, every soul, and the Beloved is the Divine. When the Gurus write as brides, they write as anyone who longs for the One. That's why the Lavan, on ang 773 and 774, can be sung at a wedding and still be about something bigger: the rounds walk a soul, step by step, toward union with God. Two people walk them together, but the journey in the words belongs to each of them. So follow the puzzle to its end. If the deepest union in Sikh thought is the soul with the One, then a single person isn't waiting outside the main story. She's already in it. To be honest about it, Sikh teaching honors married, householder life, and the aunties aren't wrong to love a wedding. But a full place in the sangat was never handed out at the wedding. Bhua Kiran does langar seva every week, sings the hymns by heart, and is the first one at the hospital when anyone's sick. That's not someone in a waiting room. Simran texts her that night: you're not waiting in line. You're already the bride in every hymn.
screen: `THE BRIDE IS EVERY SOUL.` · `THE LAVAN: A SOUL WALKING TO GOD.` · `THE SINGLE ONE IS IN THE STORY.` · `A FULL PLACE, NOT HANDED OUT.` · then, large: `A FULL PLACE.`

segments.voice: Think of someone single in your life who gets the wedding question a lot: a cousin, a friend, an aunt. In your head, write them a short text that has nothing to do with marriage, what you admire in them or a plan you'd like to make together, and keep their face in mind as you breathe.
Single life. A whole life, with a full place in the sangat, the soul already the bride in every hymn.
A full place: married or single, nobody waits in the hallway of the sangat. That's today.

screen: `DAY 1682 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 56 OF 134.` → `TOMORROW: BEBE TWISTED HER ANKLE IN THE GARDEN. WHO TAKES CARE OF HER NOW?`

howItsDone: Single Sikhs take part in every part of gurdwara life, from langar seva to kirtan, and the bridal imagery of Gurbani is read as describing every soul's longing for God.
